title: What's the best way to create 3D environments in Unreal Engine?
author: Faisal_alwaal
selftext:
Hey guys,

I'm working on a game in Unreal Engine 5.9, and I've been wondering what's the best way to actually build a 3D environment from scratch?

I'm still learning, and I'm not really sure what the best approach is. Do you guys model everything in Blender? Buy assets from Fab? Or is it usually a mix of both?

My initial idea was to use ChatGPT to generate some concept art and references, then have Claude create the assets in Blender and keep improving them until I'm happy with the results.

But I'm not sure if that's the most efficient way to do it, especially since modeling in Blender can take quite a lot of time.

I'm also wondering how you guys actually start building an environment. Do you plan the whole thing first? Start with a basic layout and slowly add details? Or do you just create the assets you need as you go?

I'm mainly trying to understand what a good workflow looks like, from having an idea in your head to actually seeing it come together in Unreal.

Any advice would be appreciated.

comments.author: _HoundOfJustice
comments.body: I start small and go step by step. I do initially draw, paint and/photobash a concept art of the  environment with help of Photoshop and 3ds Max as a mix of 2D+3D technique. Before that process i first gather reference material and ideate with or without AI. Then after all of that is done i use Gaea for terrains, 3ds Max for modeling hard surface stuff, Zbrush for organic modeling and small details on models made with Max, sometimes Speedtree for vegetation and Unreal Engine for procedural content generation and scene assembly. Ofc it always depends on kind of environment so some other software come on top of those too in some cases when it comes to environment.

comments.author: VictorBuildsApps
comments.body:
I've had agents model 16 concepts in Blender, plus two new ones after that. The recorded times per model were roughly 6 to 37 minutes, not counting building the tools and the earlier attempts, and plenty still needed fixes, heads and faces especially.

For my current game I ended up mixing it: Tripo for the character bases, Meshy for the static props, then cleanup in Blender and rigging the characters there. Simple architecture and moving parts like doors got scripted in Blender.

comments.author: teejayaiartdirector
comments.body: Procedural just use a video as reference.
